summary: Independent review of feat/compact-score-grid-0.26.1 (175c3c1) against main 5253d13 (0.26.0); builder is builder-subagent-2026-10-20. Values: all 641 x 169 = 108,329 cells equal the 8-significant-digit rounding of the v50 original, computed independently in Python (Decimal half-even) and in JS (toPrecision(8) and a BigInt exact rounding) with 0 disagreements between methods and 0 exact ties; max relative cell error 4.96e-8, max absolute 4.99e-9, max outcome mass error 1.17e-8 (limit 1e-6). Every non-score field and the key order (scoreDistribution -> scoreGrid in place) are identical to v50; main predictions.js body equals the v50 block. ?v=8850a2ae9237674d = sha256[:16] of the file in both pages. Re-running compact_predictions.py (standard library only, no time/random/env input; PYTHONHASHSEED and LC_ALL varied) reproduces the file byte for byte. Page code: the only changes in index.html / index.en.html are the ?v= and one appended expansion statement (2 lines each); embedded simulation module equals the shared pixel-simulation.js and is byte-identical to main; the expansion runs synchronously before the only scoreDistribution use (mount); a second run is a no-op. Simulation (own harness, module and expansion extracted from the branch page): 641 x 200 seeds = 128,200 and 641 x 1000 = 641,000 draws, outcome differences 0, score differences 0, full-result differences 0. Negative controls detected differences (swap 1:0/2:0: 13,724 per 641,000; mass-preserving relative 1e-3 move: 404; relative 1e-5 move: 5). Analytic bound: worst per-draw disagreement 6.3e-8, expected differences over 641,000 draws about 0.011, so 0 is the expected count. check_release PASS (1696 files) and FAIL on all 13 tamper cases with and without the manifest check. test:server 22, check-vercel 5 (dist predictions.js = repo file), analysis 15, report 14, odds PASS (877). Browser (Google Chrome 155, ko/en x 390/1440, main vs branch): 10 compared text fields incl. 41 seeded played simulations identical, screenshots byte-identical, page errors 0, no horizontal overflow (documentElement.clientWidth). Sizes in SPEC/CHANGELOG are exact; SPEC mixes decimal MB and MiB under one "MB" label. No blocker. Verdict: merge-ready with follow-ups (unit wording; production Vercel hash/transfer/screen check after deploy). publication_manifest.json was not regenerated by the reviewer and must be regenerated after this report commit. DONE means the review was performed, not final approval.

issues.description: docs/SPEC-0.26.1.md: the purpose line and the "형식 후보와 측정값" table label everything "MB" but raw sizes are decimal MB (6.79 = 6,789,268 B / 1e6; 2.13) while transfer sizes are MiB (1.47 = 1,535,945 B / 2^20; 0.70 = 722,824 / 2^20; decimal would be 1.54 and 0.72). Only the results section explains the MiB case. CHANGELOG uses decimal MB consistently (6.79 -> 2.13, Korean first visit 1.83 -> 1.02, which match gzip-6 sums 1,834,190 -> 1,021,143) but says only "gzip" without the level. Numbers are correct; units should be stated (MB = 10^6 B, gzip-6) so readers do not compare 1.47 with 1.83 as the same unit. The candidate table A/C figures are pre-implementation estimates of non-adopted options; my rebuild gives A 3.06 MB / gzip-6 1.13 MiB and C 1.33 MB (1.32 MB with the scoreGrid key) vs the stated 1.27 MB; no effect on the adopted file.

check_release.py compares non-score fields with Python == (True == 1, 1 == 1.0). Measured: with a generator edit that writes model_accepted 1 instead of true, regenerated file and updated ?v=, check_release (manifest check bypassed) PASSES; npm run test:server FAILS (deepStrictEqual, "model_accepted"). So the combined gate catches it; check_release alone would not. Optional hardening: compare json.dumps of each field.

The page expansion trusts scoreGrid length/content. Measured with the page module: 170 cells or a null cell -> validate throws -> panel shows the invalid-probabilities message; a middle cell dropped -> mass check throws; the last cell (12:12) dropped -> passes silently (mass change < 1e-6); scoreGrid missing or not an array -> passes with scoreFromModel=false (fixed 1:0 / 1:1 / 0:1 scores, no message). The published file is gated by check_release and test:server, so this only matters if an unchecked file is deployed.

After expansion scoreDistribution is the last key of each prediction (v50: position 16 of 18, before goal_model_id and score_summary). No page code depends on key order (mount reads fields by name), and the file itself keeps the v50 position. Informational.

If predictions.js fails to load, main and branch behave identically (measured in Chrome: 1 page error "Cannot read properties of undefined (reading predictions)", fixture list renders, simulation panel silently absent). The 0.26.0 follow-up (explicit load-failure message) remains open; not introduced here.

Random-seed comparison has little power for 5e-8 cell changes: the analytic expected number of score differences across 641,000 draws is about 0.011, so "0 differences" is the expected result and the cell-level value checks are the real evidence. The harness itself is sensitive (relative 1e-5 mass-preserving perturbation -> 5 differences in 641,000).

Not verified: production/preview Vercel deployment (served predictions.js hash, brotli transfer size, which SPEC notes was larger than gzip for 0.26.0, screens). Also a deploy-time skew where a stale cached 0.26.0 HTML (no expansion) receives the new predictions.js (query string ignored by static hosting) would show the invalid-probabilities message in the simulation panel; with Vercel default must-revalidate caching this should be brief, but it was not measured.

publication_manifest.json (builder file) was not regenerated; it must be regenerated after this report and the review screenshots are committed, otherwise check_release fails on the manifest. During the review macOS denied this process access to the Desktop folder (EPERM on every read, including the Read tool) after the browser run started; all later work used the scratch worktrees (same commit 175c3c1; predictions.js byte-identical).
